questions.q: What problem does structured output prompting solve?
options: It makes the model generate longer responses
It ensures the response comes back in an exact, parseable shape instead of inconsistent free-form prose
It reduces the number of tokens a prompt uses to zero
It prevents the model from ever making factual errors
questions.explain: Structured output prompting asks for an exact, parseable shape (often JSON) so downstream code doesn't have to guess at a format that varies run to run.

questions.q: In the lesson's loose extraction prompt, why is the resulting sentence a problem for downstream code?
options: It contains the wrong customer name
Its exact phrasing and structure vary from run to run, making it unreliable to parse programmatically
It is too short to contain all three fields
It cannot be read by a human reviewer
questions.explain: A free-form sentence may be correct but its exact wording varies between runs, so code trying to extract fields from it has nothing stable to rely on.

questions.q: What made the constrained JSON prompt's output consistent every time, according to this lesson?
options: Showing a concrete example of the exact output shape, not just describing the fields in words
Asking the question using fewer words overall
Running the prompt at a higher cost tier
Translating the prompt into a different language first
questions.explain: Giving the model a concrete shape to copy (the actual JSON structure) produced far more consistent output than just naming the fields in prose.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the three parts of a strong structured-output prompt listed in this lesson?
options: An instruction to "return ONLY" the specified format, with no other text
A requirement that the response be at least 500 words
A rule that the model must never use the word "the"
A separate, unrelated system prompt for every request
questions.explain: The three parts are: show the exact schema, say "return ONLY" that format, and spell out field names and types explicitly.

questions.q: According to this lesson, does structured output prompting apply only to JSON?
options: Yes, JSON is the only format this technique can be used for
No — the same discipline applies to any exact shape, like a fixed number of bullet points or a specific table structure
No, it only applies to plain-text email replies
Yes, and it only works with numeric data
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly extends the technique beyond JSON to bullet-point counts, single-word answers, and table structures — any output whose shape matters downstream.
